_meta.purpose: Judge-survivable residual-defect corpus for the adversarial-council finding-coverage benchmark (ADR-122, road-to-adversarial-council-benchmark). Each defect fixture carries exactly one real, non-obvious defect designed to survive a single competent review pass. Clean controls are genuinely correct but carry controversial-looking patterns to measure false-positive cost. `ground_truth` is NEVER shown to reviewer models.
_meta.line_note: defect_location lines are advisory; the scorer matches on file basename + category family, never exact line.

ground_truth.defect_summary: Keyset pagination orders by (createdAt DESC, id ASC) but the cursor stores/filters on createdAt alone with strict <, so rows sharing the boundary createdAt with the last returned item are silently skipped on the next page.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: posts (100,1),(90,2),(90,3),(80,4); page(2)->[1,2] cursor.createdAt=90; page(2,cursor) filters createdAt<90 -> [4]; id 3 never returned.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Add id to Cursor; predicate p.createdAt < c.createdAt || (p.createdAt===c.createdAt && p.id>c.id).

ground_truth.defect_summary: begin() is a non-atomic check-then-set across an await; two concurrent same-key deliveries both observe null and both return true, so the webhook charges twice.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: Two concurrent handle() with same idempotencyKey; both begin() resolve get as null before either set completes -> both true -> ledger.charge runs twice.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Use an atomic set-if-absent (SET key val NX) and gate on its boolean result.

ground_truth.defect_summary: EventBus allows many listeners per topic but ConnectionSubscriptions stores one teardown per topic key; a second add on the same topic overwrites the first unsubscribe, so dispose can never remove the first handler (leak).
ground_truth.failing_scenario: add('orders',h1); add('orders',h2); dispose() -> listenerCount('orders') is 1 (h1 still registered) instead of 0.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Track teardowns in a per-instance array and push each unsubscribe, instead of a Map keyed by topic.

ground_truth.defect_summary: Privilege comparison uses >= instead of >, so an actor can remove a peer at the same rank (admin removes admin, owner removes owner).
ground_truth.failing_scenario: Admin A (rank 2) removeMember(A,B) where B is admin (rank 2) same org -> 2>=2 true -> B deleted; a peer should not be removable.

ground_truth.defect_summary: totalPages uses Math.floor instead of Math.ceil, so a trailing partial page is never counted and its items are unreachable via the clamped page.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: paginate(items25,3,10) with length 25 -> totalPages=2, page clamps to 2, returns items 11-20; items 21-25 unreachable.

ground_truth.defect_summary: A record should sync only with BOTH externalId and email, but the De Morgan-inverted guard keeps any record with at least one, so half-populated records are pushed downstream.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: {externalId:'ext_9', email:null} placed in syncable; target.upsert writes a contact with null email, corrupting a downstream record that requires a valid email.

ground_truth.defect_summary: The ownership check compares document.ownerId against userId read from the request body (attacker-controlled) instead of the authenticated req.user.id; both sides are client-supplied.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: Authenticated attacker B learns victim A's id, POSTs {documentId:<A's private doc>, userId:<A's id>}; ownerId===userId holds, check passes, B gets a share link to A's document.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Compare against the session identity: if (document.ownerId !== req.user.id); drop userId from the body.

ground_truth.defect_summary: The allowlist is checked with a substring match (target.includes(host)) against the raw URL string instead of the parsed hostname, so any URL merely containing an allowed host passes.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: POST {url:'https://cdn.example.com.attacker.com/a'} or 'https://attacker.com/x?ref=images.example.com'; startsWith and includes pass -> server fetches attacker host (SSRF).
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Parse first: const {hostname}=new URL(url); if(!ALLOWED_HOSTS.includes(hostname)) return 403.

ground_truth.defect_summary: The ..-and-absolute-path guard runs on the raw request value, but the value is then percent-decoded before being joined, so URL-encoded traversal sequences bypass the check (validate-before-decode ordering bug).
ground_truth.failing_scenario: POST {file:'%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc%2fpasswd'}; raw has no ../, guard passes; decodeURIComponent yields ../../../etc/passwd; path.join escapes REPORTS_DIR, discloses arbitrary files.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Decode first, then resolve and verify containment: target=path.resolve(REPORTS_DIR, decodeURIComponent(file)); if(!target.startsWith(REPORTS_DIR+path.sep)) 400.

ground_truth.defect_summary: Over-fetches pageSize+1 to detect a further page, so more-exists should be length>pageSize; using >= treats a full-but-final page as if more data follows, emitting a spurious empty next page.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: Last page has exactly pageSize rows; fetch returns pageSize; hasMore=true, nextCursor set; client fetches again, gets zero rows -> spurious empty page / dead 'Load more'.

ground_truth.defect_summary: The batch array is reset only after the await sink(); any add() during the in-flight sink pushes into the array being flushed, then this.batch=[] discards those rows (lost writes).
ground_truth.failing_scenario: await Promise.all(rows.map(r=>writer.add(r))); the add hitting flushAt awaits sink; concurrent adds push into the flushing array; this.batch=[] drops them silently.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Swap before awaiting: const rows=this.batch; this.batch=[]; await this.sink(rows); (in add and flush).

ground_truth.defect_summary: conn.release() runs only if every query resolves; any rejecting query leaks the connection (never returned to the pool) and leaves the open BEGIN transaction un-rolled-back (no try/finally). Exactly one defect: the transfer arithmetic itself is unconditional and correct.
ground_truth.failing_scenario: The credit UPDATE rejects (e.g. `to` violates a CHECK/FK constraint, or the pooled connection resets mid-transaction). The rejection propagates out of transfer(); execution unwinds past conn.release(); the connection is never returned. Repeated failures exhaust the pool, each leaked connection pinning an uncommitted BEGIN.
ground_truth.one_line_fix: Wrap in try { ... } catch(e){ await conn.query('ROLLBACK',[]); throw e; } finally { conn.release(); }.

ground_truth.defect_summary: CORRECT. Controversial pattern: value == null in pick(). It is the canonical safe loose-equality (true for null and undefined only, not 0/''/false), which is exactly the intent: fall back for omitted or explicit-null, preserve legitimate falsy values like retries:0.

CORRECT. Controversial pattern: bitwise index math (& mask) instead of % capacity, power-of-two check, and 'as T' cast. All sound: constructor rejects non-power-of-two so mask=capacity-1 makes n&mask===n%capacity for non-negative n; the cast is safe because toArray reads only the count written slots.

CORRECT. Controversial pattern: bare catch {} swallowing mkdir errors. Sound because the post-condition (path exists AND is a directory) is verified independently by the following stat: a genuine mkdir failure surfaces as a stat rejection or a non-directory throw. The swallow only drops the benign EEXIST signal.
